findings.title: Round 9's shared read-back cache races. A verification handed a spend can crash in its locked prune after its ticket is gone, so a later verification decides on the rollback and the executed action is dispatched again.
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:473 `current._readback = self._readback` gives every in-flight snapshot the follower's one cache dict. owners.py:389 `self._readback[key] = cached` inserts into it with no lock (the read-back is unlocked since round 9, owners.py:416). owners.py:418-421 discards the ticket (419), then iterates that same dict to prune it (421), with the lock held. A concurrent insert makes the comprehension raise RuntimeError('dictionary changed size during iteration'). The raise comes before the comparison loop (owners.py:423-443), so the observation is never recorded, and the ticket is already discarded. pinned() wraps only self._follow() (owners.py:469-472), so the RuntimeError escapes. _Memo keeps it as the pin error (authority.py:381-394), and Authorities.check catches only OwnerUnavailable/WorldRefused (authority.py:288-293), so it escapes gateway.admit/dispatch. Measured results. p10 (4 threads × 150 pins, a changing set of 30 experiment accounts): c69e579 gave 8/600 RuntimeError, ceaf8cd 0/600. p10c through ExecutionDesk.gateway().admit with 4 threads: 131 FEASIBLE, 16 MISSING_INFORMATION, 13 raised RuntimeError. p17 forces the interleaving with sys.settrace in one thread, the scheduling control round 8's B p03 used. The setup is an in-place spend by the executor, a verification T2 handed the spend, an object-replacing restore, and a campaign set that gains one experiment account at the restore. T2 raised RuntimeError, the re-dispatch went through, and the executor was called 2 times. The same interleaving without the new account (NEW_ACCOUNT=0): T2 MISSING_INFORMATION, re-dispatch refused, executor called 1 time. This falsifies README §4:160-161, owners.py:322-324 and owners.py:414 ('no verification decides until every earlier one has been compared'), and §9:449-450 lists it as fixed.

findings.why: Round 9 added the ticket rule so that a spend an earlier verification was handed is never overtaken by a rollback, and it narrowed the documented residual to 'a state no verification was handed' or 'an accounts() that raises'. In this case T2 was handed the spend and its read-back succeeded. Its observation is still lost because of a race round 9 introduced: moving the read-back out of the lock while keeping one mutable cache shared with the locked step. The outcome is the B8-m1 outcome, which round 8's lens F and critic held as a Q4 PARTIAL reason: an executed action is re-dispatched on a rolled-back account, and the executor runs twice. The crash also turns a refusal into an uncaught exception at the Mind-facing gateway, which is not recordable. It needs three things at once: concurrency, an object-replacing restore, and a change in the account set landing inside the prune. That is narrow, so this is graded MINOR in line with B8-m1's precedent, but skeptics should weigh it.
findings.fix: Do not let unlocked writers share the dict the locked step iterates. Either give each snapshot its own cache (a copy taken at the pin) and adopt the pruned result under the lock, or prune from an atomic copy (self._readback.copy()). Record the observations (the comparison loop) before anything else in the locked step can raise, and keep the ticket in flight until the comparison has completed. Add p17 (settrace-forced) as a deterministic control and p10 as a stress control.

findings.question: Q4 (availability; theoretical). Not a PARTIAL reason.
findings.title: pinned() sets the re-entrancy flag and takes its ticket before entering the try whose finally resets them. A KeyboardInterrupt during _ticket()'s lock wait refuses that thread for good, with a false 'read through' message.
findings.evidence: owners.py:466-468: `self._in_follow.active = True` and `ticket = self._ticket()` run before `try:` (468); the finally is at 476-479. Python's Lock.acquire is interruptible by signals. p14 simulates another verification's comparison by holding the private _lock from a thread, then sends SIGINT while the main thread waits in _ticket(). The first pin was interrupted. Every later read on that thread then gave 'OwnerUnavailable: the execution side read through the budget reader it feeds while the reader was asking for ...'. Another thread still read revision 1. An asynchronous exception between `_in_flight.add` and the return of _ticket (owners.py:452-455) would leak a ticket and refuse every thread.

findings.title: The ticket rule orders verifications by when they start, not by when they are handed their accounts. A verification that started earlier but is handed the rollback later still decides on the rollback while a later-started verification holding the spend is in flight. README §4 states the guarantee without that qualifier.
findings.evidence: owners.py:420 `earlier = any(t < ticket for t in self._in_flight)` refuses a comparison only while a LOWER ticket is in flight. The ticket is taken at owners.py:467, before `self._follow()` at 470, so the order of tickets is not the order of hand-over. README §4:159-161 says 'the earlier one may carry a later state, so a spend a verification was handed is never overtaken by a rollback a later verification reads', and §9:449-450 lists R9-C-F4 / F9-4 / K9-F1 as fixed. The §4 residual list (182-184) names only 'a state no verification was handed'. The only control, test_authority_review_r9.py:54-78, covers the case where the verification holding the spend started first.
findings.reproduction: Static reading; not executed. Mirror test_authority_review_r9.py:54 as follows. (1) Dispatch once (calls=1). (2) Start the re-dispatch on thread T1. Its accounts() blocks for T1 before reading the mapping, so T1 holds ticket N. (3) Replace the ledger with the spent copy. (4) Start T2 = reader.pinned() with ticket N+1. It is handed the spent ledger and paused after `_read_back`, before it compares (the same monkeypatch the r8 B8-m1 test uses). (5) Restore `before` and release T1. T1 is handed `before` and compares. Its only in-flight peer has ticket N+1 > N, so `earlier` is False, history h equals seen, T1 decides, and the re-admitted digest is unchanged. Expected: executor calls == 2 (the B8-m1 / R9-C-F4 outcome). Then T2 records h+[c], and the restored account is 'behind' from then on.
findings.why: The round-9 claim reads as closing the B8-m1 class whenever some verification was handed the spend first. It closes it only when that verification also started first. The remaining window is undisclosed and has no control.
findings.fix: Either (a) take a hand-over mark right after accounts() returns (under the lock, `mark = self._tickets`) and refuse, for that verification only, while ANY other in-flight ticket <= mark exists. This covers every verification handed accounts before this one and subsumes the earlier-ticket rule. Or (b) qualify README §4:159-161, §9:449-450, owners.py:319-324 and the r9 test name with 'started earlier', and add this window to the §4 residual list. Either way, add the mirrored interleaving above as a deterministic control.

Each hung verification's ticket also stays in flight, so later ones are refused 'still in flight'.

Nothing stops this data: ScientificExperiment.metadata is a plain dict (experiment.py:193, 329), and BudgetCharge.detail is unvalidated (budget.py:113, 130). These outcomes contradict README §4:175-176 ('An account no verification reads (unreadable, not plain data, ...) refuses nothing'), owners.py:316-318, and §4:169-170 ('refuse each other transiently'). findings.title: Introduced in round 9: the unlocked read-back writes into the shared read-back cache dict while another verification's locked prune iterates that same dict.

The lock serializes only the comparisons, not the writers. If one thread inserts a new account key while another is iterating, CPython raises RuntimeError ('dictionary changed size during iteration'). That error escapes `_observe_all`, is kept by `_Memo._pin_now` (authority.py:383-387), and is re-raised at a budget read. It is not caught by Authorities.check (294-297), admit, or authorize_dispatch's except tuple (admission.py:421). The failed verification's observations, possibly a spend, are not recorded.
findings.reproduction: Static reading; not executed. The race needs two concurrent pins and a newly handed account key (the rotating-account pattern of test_authority_review_r9.py:145). It is nondeterministic and low probability.
findings.why: Round 8 read back under the lock, so this race did not exist. The outcome is an unrecorded exception instead of a refusal, and the lost observation can widen E10-F1's window.
findings.fix: Prune over a snapshot of the items (`list(self._readback.items())`), or perform the cache write under `self._lock`.

Code at c69e579:

- An experiment is checked with `_plain(exp.to_dict())` before it is read back (owners.py:376-379).

- So any evaluation whose metadata holds a nested list or dict makes the whole experiment "not plain". This includes every such experiment restored from JSON through the owner's own from_dict. The owner itself serializes these values and reads them back without trouble.

The wrong outcome:
1. The spend is handed to a verification, refused, and never recorded.
2. After an object-replacing restore (the restore model the BudgetReader docstring names for sria.campaign), the restored history equals the observed one.
3. The restored state is accepted, and the already executed AdmittedAction is dispatched again. The executor ran twice.

This contradicts README §4:165-166: "a return to an earlier state never re-authorizes what the account had moved past". The control and ceaf8cd both show that the designed behaviour is a refusal.

It is outside the documented residuals:
- README:182-184 covers only "a state no verification was handed" and an accounts() that raises. Here the state was handed, and accounts() returned normally.
- README:175-176 ("an account no verification reads ... refuses nothing") is about accounts that no world binds.
- The plain-data residual covers refusing the unreadable state, not re-authorizing the restore.

It is a regression from round 9: ceaf8cd refuses every variant, nested metadata and the numpy-ledger cases included. It needs no concurrency and no introspection, and uses only public paths, including the Mind port with an LM suggestion (c1010). The r9 plain-data test sets only experiment-level metadata (test_authority_review_r9.py:125-141), which is a plain dict, so no control covers this case.

Severity is MAJOR, not BLOCKER, for three reasons:
- At-most-once execution is a documented residual of the execution owner.
- This outcome class (B5-F1) was graded MAJOR before.
- An admission the Mind makes on the restored state is consistent with the owners' current statement.
It is a reproduced bypass of the forward-only guard, and a materially false README claim for ordinary content, under Q4.

- My v02 probe shows that the general "unreadable handed spend is not recorded" mechanism predates round 9 for content that is not JSON-serializable (set, datetime, Decimal, bytes, re-dispatched at both SHAs). Rounds 1-9 missed this, and fix item (3) in the finding addresses it. What is new in round 9 is reaching it with ordinary, owner-readable content: nested evaluation metadata, int-keyed nested metadata, and a numpy iteration or predicted on a ledger. That new part is what makes this MAJOR.
